research_question: What structural constraint may shape the next phase of AI infrastructure expansion?

reasoning_items.text: AI infrastructure expansion is increasingly connected to access to large, reliable power supply.
Grid interconnection and power availability can constrain how quickly new compute capacity is deployed.
If compute hardware becomes easier to source while power remains location constrained, infrastructure advantage may shift toward energy procurement and site access.
Regions with available generation and faster interconnection may attract a larger share of new AI infrastructure.

critical_unknowns.text: How quickly grid interconnection queues will clear.
Whether power procurement constraints persist as new generation comes online.

research_question: How could tighter chip export controls reshape supply chains?

reasoning_items.text: Export restrictions alter which suppliers and destinations can transact directly.
Buyers may diversify toward alternative chip suppliers or architectures if access to restricted accelerators becomes less certain.

critical_unknowns.text: How broadly the restrictions will be enforced across intermediaries.
